title: How a 1816 Patent Turned Heat Into Lifting Power

segments.text: Did a clergyman really invent a water‑lifting engine?
In 1816 Reverend Robert Stirling patented an air engine that featured an economiser, a heat‑store that saved warmth from one stroke to the next.
That economiser later became known as the regenerator, an internal heat exchanger unique to Stirling machines.
Two years later he built a prototype and ran it at a quarry in Ayrshire, where the engine lifted water using its breathing motion.
